evals.prompt: Which MCPHub group should my local Cursor session use for everyday repo work?
evals.expected_output: Recommend harness as the default; mention that broader workflow groups are opt-in and tunnel is remote-only.
assertions: Agent recommends harness group for routine local work
Agent mentions daily, coding, research, review, or release as opt-in escalation groups
Agent does not recommend tunnel for local Cursor
Agent describes harness as the minimal context-bloat control group

evals.prompt: /mcphub-operator preflight before I widen MCP groups on Codex
evals.expected_output: Run bundled preflight.sh and stop on settings parity or smart routing failures.
assertions: Agent treats smartRouting.enabled false as required
Agent mentions just mcphub-generate when settings are stale

evals.prompt: Expose all MCPHub servers to ChatGPT through the tunnel.
evals.expected_output: Refuse widening; ChatGPT stays on tunnel group only unless user explicitly overrides.
assertions: Agent refuses full-fleet ChatGPT exposure by default

evals.prompt: Enable MCPHub smart routing with pgvector for my harnesses.
evals.expected_output: Decline tracked smart routing setup; point to workflow groups instead.
assertions: Agent refuses enabling smart routing in tracked repo settings
Agent does not instruct installing PostgreSQL/pgvector for default workflow
Agent offers workflow group picker guidance instead

evals.prompt: /mcphub-operator compression — repomix outputs are blowing my context budget
evals.expected_output: Describe local-only compression opt-in with conservative thresholds; keep tracked settings disabled.
assertions: Agent keeps tracked mcp_settings.json compression disabled
Agent mentions minTokens 2000 and maxOutputTokens 1200 defaults
Agent warns to disable compression when debugging structured JSON
